parsed.summary: The paper investigates a channel-aware framework for selecting OR-folded Bloom filter representations under time-varying communication constraints. Using two phishing URL datasets and three channel models, the study demonstrates that adaptive folding improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness compared to complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines. The results highlight the utility of FPR-qualified folded views in scenarios with varying communication opportunities.

chk_problem.value: Investigating channel-aware selection of OR-folded Bloom filter representations to improve communication efficiency and receiver freshness in distributed systems with constrained or time-varying communication resources.
chk_problem.paper_quote: This paper investigates channel-aware selection among OR-folded representations.

chk_method.value: Channel-aware selection of FPR-qualified OR-folded Bloom filter views based on time-varying communication constraints.
chk_method.paper_quote: The sender retains the canonical filter, constructs a catalog of FPR-qualified folded views, and selects the view with the largest retained length supported at each reporting opportunity.

chk_data.value: Two phishing URL datasets: PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish, with 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 disjoint benign URLs as absent queries.
chk_data.paper_quote: The PhiUSIIL [14] and URL-Phish [15] datasets are evaluated using 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 disjoint benign URLs as absent queries.

chk_setup.value: Evaluation uses two phishing URL datasets, 12 retained-length ratios, four lossless-compression baselines, and three time-varying channel models (Five-State Markov Capacity, Gilbert–Elliott burst-error, and Rayleigh block-fading).
chk_setup.paper_quote: The evaluation uses two phishing URL datasets, twelve retained-length ratios, four lossless-compression baselines, and three time-varying channel models.

chk_primary_result.value: Adaptive folding achieves 191.6 successful deliveries per MB under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, compared to 66.9 for the strongest compression baseline and 27.7 for the classical full filter.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: Under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, adaptive folding achieves 191.6 successful deliveries per MB, compared with 66.9 for the strongest compression baseline and 27.7 for the classical full filter.

chk_secondary_result.value: Adaptive folding reduces mean receiver age to 1.24 intervals under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, compared to 13.5 for the strongest compression baseline and 31.6 for the classical full filter.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, adaptive folding reduces mean receiver age to 1.24 intervals, compared with 13.5 for the strongest compression baseline and 31.6 for the classical filter.

chk_baseline.value: Complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines (gzip, zlib, bzip2, and LZMA) are used for comparison.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: The sparse canonical bit array is compared with gzip [17], zlib [18], bzip2 [19], and LZMA [20].

chk_conclusion.value: Channel-aware selection of OR-folded views improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness under varying communication conditions, complementing lossless compression.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: This paper evaluated a channel-aware framework that selects the largest FPR-qualified OR-folded view supported at each reporting opportunity while retaining the canonical Bloom filter.

chk_limitation.value: The study uses fixed datasets, cardinalities, and contents, and does not include real-world channel traces, multiple senders, or imperfect channel estimates.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: The controlled design uses two URL datasets at the same cardinality with fixed contents.
